note: Crimea and Sevastopol are shown as part of Ukraine. They have been administered by the Russian Federation since 2014; the UN General Assembly has not recognised the annexation.
The Golan Heights are shown as occupied Syrian territory. Israel extended its jurisdiction there in 1981; the Security Council declared that step without legal effect.

The northern part of the island has been administered since 1974 by the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, which the UN does not recognise. The UN treats the area as part of Cyprus, separated by a buffer zone under the UNFICYP mission.
Somaliland declared independence in 1991 and governs itself. No state and no UN body has recognised it; the UN lists the territory as part of Somalia.
basis: UN practice; Somaliland is neither a member nor an observer state

label: Kosovo
note: Kosovo's status remains undetermined for the UN. The territory falls under resolution 1244 and Kosovo is not a UN member state; its 2008 declaration of independence is recognised by some states and rejected by Serbia and others.

label: Western Sahara
note: Western Sahara is on the UN list of Non-Self-Governing Territories and still awaits a referendum on self-determination. Morocco controls most of it, the Polisario Front the remainder. The UN does not treat it as part of Morocco.
basis: UN list of Non-Self-Governing Territories (Charter, Chapter XI); General Assembly resolution 1514 (XV)

label: Palestine
note: The State of Palestine holds non-member observer state status at the UN. Its borders remain subject to negotiation and part of the territory is under Israeli administration.

label: Taiwan
note: Taiwan governs itself. Since resolution 2758 the UN has not treated it as a separate state and recognises the government in Beijing as the representative of China. The Atlas maps it separately because its society and its data differ from mainland China.
basis: UN General Assembly resolution 2758 (1971); this is a deliberate departure from UN practice
